chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abdul-Mumin al-Ansari that Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
God, the Mighty and Majestic, has granted the believer three qualities: nobility in the world through his religion; prosperity in the Hereafter; and dignity in the hearts of all people.
ai.seo_question: What are the three qualities God grants to believers according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a tripartite structure of divine favor, linking internal spiritual integrity with external social influence. The 'awe in the hearts of the world' (al-mahaba) reflects the Shia concept of *wilayah* and the believer's dignified presence, while 'success in the hereafter' (al-falaj) emphasizes ultimate deliverance from divine punishment. This narration underscores the holistic nature of faith, where inner piety manifests as tangible respect in the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-157 Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abdul-Mumin al-Ansari that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said, “
God has granted three things to believers: nobility in the world and his religion; prosperity in the Hereafter; and dignity in the hearts of the people of the world.”
